chosen.premise: Primeape can become so angry that it dies, yet its face looks peaceful after death.
chosen.hook: Primeape’s anger can literally kill it.
chosen.visualIdea: Primeape’s rage meter fills past maximum, then cuts to its unexpectedly peaceful expression.
chosen.note: An unusually dark, concrete claim with an excellent reversal: death makes Primeape look peaceful. One official entry fully supports the premise and gives the episode a strong visual arc.

candidates.hook: Primeape’s anger can literally kill it.
candidates.visualIdea: Primeape’s rage meter fills past maximum, then cuts to its unexpectedly peaceful expression.
candidates.note: An unusually dark, concrete claim with an excellent reversal: death makes Primeape look peaceful. One official entry fully supports the premise and gives the episode a strong visual arc.

candidates.premise: Seeing Primeape’s eyes angers it, running makes it angrier, and defeating it makes it angrier still.
candidates.hook: Against Primeape, every possible response makes things worse.
candidates.visualIdea: A branching choice screen shows look, run, or fight—all routes ending with a larger rage meter.
candidates.note: The escalating decision-tree mechanic is highly specific and strongly supported. It is slightly less surprising than the death premise because Primeape’s relentless pursuit is already well known.

candidates.premise: Primeape only stops being angry when nobody is around, making its peaceful side almost impossible to witness.
candidates.hook: Primeape has a calm mode—but you can’t watch it happen.
candidates.visualIdea: A camera approaches a calm Primeape; the instant it notices the lens, its expression flips to rage.
candidates.note: A strong contradiction built from multiple entries: Primeape has a calm state that observation prevents. The premise is visually clear, though the payoff is less startling than its fatal rage.

candidates.premise: Primeape’s fury boosts blood flow and muscle strength, but makes it much less intelligent.
candidates.hook: What if getting stronger also made Primeape dumber?
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen Primeape: its muscles grow as a thought bubble shrinks into confused scribbles.
candidates.note: A sharply defined biological tradeoff, directly supported by two Pokédex entries. The strength-versus-intelligence contrast is compelling, though the basic rage-power trope is somewhat familiar.

candidates.premise: Primeape reaches its final evolution not by leveling up, but by using a move.
candidates.hook: Primeape’s final evolution breaks the usual level-up pattern.
candidates.visualIdea: Primeape uses a move, then transforms into Annihilape as a Ghost type appears beside Fighting.
candidates.note: A clear, highly visual evolution mechanic and a useful connection to Annihilape. It is well supported by the supplied evolution data, but the method is from a trusted secondary source rather than an official Pokédex entry.

candidates.premise: Researchers theorize Primeape may remain angry even while sealed inside a Poké Ball.
candidates.hook: Primeape might still be furious inside its Poké Ball.
candidates.visualIdea: A Poké Ball sits still while an interior cutaway reveals Primeape raging beside a calm-looking exterior.
candidates.note: A fun unsettling image, but the key claim is explicitly only a researcher theory. The brain-health entry supports constant rage generally, not that rage continues inside a Poké Ball.

rounds.request: Not applicable: “anger-can-kill-it” is strong enough to lead the episode. Stronger alternatives would need an equally specific contradiction or consequence, direct support from an official entry, and a visual payoff that is more surprising than Primeape’s rage literally ending in death and peace.
